This regular second appeal filed by the appellants challenging the judgment and decree dated 24.07.2020 passed in R.A.No.64/2015 by the learned Principal District NC: 2024:KHC:45699 and Sessions Judge, Davanagere and the judgment and decree dated 28.04.2015 passed in O.S.No.123/2014 by the III Additional Senior Civil Judge, Davanagere.
2. For convenience, the parties are referred to according to their ranking before the trial Court.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellants were the plaintiffs, and the respondents were the defendants.

3. Brief facts leading rise to the filing of this appeal are as follows:
The plaintiffs filed a suit against the defendants for declaration of title and consequential relief of permanent injunction and alternative relief of possession of the suit property.
Initially, the land bearing Sy.No.64 of Shiramagondanahalli in Davanagere Taluk was owned and possessed by Narappa S/o Jadhav Hanumanthappa, measuring 31 acres and 31 guntas.
To discharge the debt, he had sold the property in favour of one K.M. Gurushanthayya, i.e., husband of plaintiff No.1 and father of other plaintiffs.

He purchased the said property under a NC:
2024:KHC:45699 registered sale deed dated 09.07.1969.

After the demise of K.M.
Gurushanthayya, the property was transferred in the plaintiffs' name.

5 No.4 issued a gazette notification proposing the acquisition of agricultural lands bearing Sy.No.64/1A2, 64/1A3, etc., allotting the same to the applicants.

sentences.text: The said gazette notification was issued in 1982.
In the gazette notification, it is mentioned that N.Rudrappa S/o Puttappa and Kotrappa S/o Veerappa and Khatedars and Anubhavidhars of Sy.No.64/1A2, 64/1A3.
It is contended that under the garb of acquisition, defendant No.4 acquired the agricultural lands belonging to the plaintiffs.
It is contended that no acquisition proceedings are initiated regarding suit schedule property.
There was no occasion for defendant No.4 to pass any award regarding payment of compensation for such acquisition.
Hence, no award was passed by defendant No.4.
Before passing an award, no notice was issued by defendant No.4 to the plaintiffs or the deceased K.M. Gurushanthayya.
Defendant No.4 has not taken possession of the suit schedule property.

Defendant No.4 NC:
2024:KHC:45699 is putting a high-handed claim that possession of the suit schedule property belonging to the plaintiffs was taken; as such, the claim made by defendant No.4 has no legal sanction.
Based on an untenable claim, defendant Nos.3 and 4 claim to have allowed defendant No.6 to enclose the suit schedule property.
The plaintiffs were issued a legal notice calling upon the defendants to rectify their mistake and to remove the enclosure put up around the suit schedule property.
Defendant Nos.1 to 4 failed to do so.
Hence, a cause of action arose for the plaintiffs to file a suit for declaration of title, consequential relief of permanent injunction and alternative relief of possession.
4. Despite service of summons, Defendant Nos.1 and 2, failed to appear before the trial Court.
They were placed exparte.
Defendant No.5 appeared, but did not file the written statement.
Defendant Nos.3 and 4 filed a joint written statement denying the allegation made in the plaint.

It is contended that as per Government notification, they have acquired a total of 4 acres of land NC:
2024:KHC:45699 out of Sy.Nos.64/1A, 64/1A3 and 64/1B as per the provisions of Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board (for short 'KIADB Act, 1966').
They have taken possession of the acquired property and paid the compensation to the land owners and allotted the said lands to the applicants by forming the sites.
The suit filed by the plaintiffs is not maintainable, and prays to dismiss the suit.
5. Defendant No.6 filed a written statement denying the averments made in the plaint, and it is contended that the plaintiffs are not in possession of the suit schedule property.
Defendant No.4 acquired Sy.No.64/1A2 measuring 1 acre, Sy.No.64/1A3 measuring 2 acres, Sy.No.64/1B measuring 1 acre and confirmed the sites in the acquired lands.
Defendant No.4 allotted the sites bearing 18-A in favour of defendant No.6 on 19.11.1994.
The possession of the said property was delivered to defendant No.6 with specific boundaries.
Defendant No.6 constructed a rice mill in the year 1995 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:45699 and continued in possession of the said property.
Hence, prays to dismiss the suit.

7. The plaintiffs, to prove their case, plaintiff No.2 was examined as PW.1, examined 3 witnesses as PWs.2 to 4 and marked 47 documents as Exs.P1 to 47.
The defendant's side examined two witnesses as DWs.1 and 2, and marked 32 documents as Exs.D1 to 32.
The trial Court, dismissed the suit of the plaintiffs with costs vide judgment dated 28.04.2015.
The plaintiffs, aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed in O.S.No.123/2014 filed an appeal in R.A.No.64/2015 on the file of learned Principal District and Sessions Judge, Davanagere.

sentences.text: The first Appellate Court, dismissed the appeal vide judgment dated 24.07.2020 and confirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court.
The plaintiffs aggrieved by the impugned judgments, filed this regular second appeal.
Heard Sri.Gangadhar Gurumath, learned senior counsel for J.M.Umeshamurthy for the plaintiffs.

9. Learned senior counsel for the plaintiffs submits that the trial Court failed to consider the evidence of PW.1 and the boundaries of 1 acre of land sold by Narappa, and it is contended that the sale made by Narappa is not in dispute.
After the father's death of the plaintiffs, the said property devolved upon the plaintiffs by succession.
He submits that the names of the plaintiffs appeared in the record of rights.
The courts below could have drawn a presumption under Section 133 of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act regarding the entries.
The defendants failed to rebut the presumption regarding the entries, and he submits that defendant No.6 admitted the acquisition of land bearing Sy.No.64/1A2 and others.
The acquiring authority had not issued any notice to the plaintiffs's father or the plaintiffs, and further, the award passed by the land acquisition officer is behind the back of the plaintiffs.
Hence, on these grounds, he submits that the - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:45699 courts below have committed an error in passing the impugned judgments.
Accordingly, on these grounds, prays to allow the appeal.

10. Perused the records and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the plaintiffs.

The plaintiffs to substantiate their case, plaintiff No.1 was examined as PW.1.
He reiterated the plaint averments in the examination-in-chief and to establish that plaintiff's father had purchased the suit schedule property produced original sale deed marked as Ex.P1.

Exs.P27 and 28 are the certified copies of depositions, Ex.P29 is the certified copy of the memo of instructions of the plaintiff, Ex.P30 is the certified copy of the memo of instructions of the defendants, Ex.P31 is the certified copy of notice issued by Court commissioner, Exs.P32 and 33 are certified copy of report given by Court commissioner, Ex.P34 is the certified copy of sketches submitted by Court commissioner, Ex.P35 is the certified copy of sale deed dated 09.07.1969,

The plaintiffs also examined the witnesses to establish that their father purchased the suit schedule property under the registered sale deed Ex.P1.

In rebuttal, the defendants examined two witnesses DWs.1 and 2, and they have deposed that acquiring authority had not acquired the property of the plaintiffs, it is only the land bearing Sy.Nos.64/1A2, 64/1A3 etc.
Defendant No.4 issued a gazette notification and preliminary notification in 1982 dated 26.02.1982 under Section 28(1) of the KIADB Act, 1966.
The land acquisition officer passed an award.
The plaintiffs did not challenge the acquisition proceedings initiated by the acquiring authority.
The defendants have specifically contended that Sy.No.64/1A3 was not acquired by the Government and stated that there is no existence of suit schedule property on the spot.
There is a serious dispute regarding the location and identity of the property.

Further, the first Appellate Court recorded its finding that if the land belonging to the plaintiffs was acquired by KIADB, they could have approached the Special Land acquisition officer, and produced title deeds before the - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC:45699 land acquisition officer.
The plaintiffs, without approaching the Land Acquisition Officer filed the suit.
The civil Court has no jurisdiction to decide the validity of the acquisition proceedings.

13. The Courts below have concurrently recorded the finding of facts that the plaintiffs have failed to prove that they are the owners, in possession of the suit lands within the given mahazar and boundaries as succeeded from the late Gurushanthayya and the plaintiffs have proved alleged illegal acts of defendants attempting to interfere into the possession trying to dispossess and put up the construction.

Further, it was held that the plaintiffs are not entitled to possession of the suit schedule property and that defendant No.4 has acquired the suit schedule property through due Sri Basavaraj Wodeyar vs State Of Karnataka on 6 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158275115/
8 procedure, and defendant No.6 has constructed the rice mill on the site allotted to him.

sentences.text: Both the courts below have rightly appreciated the material on record and passed the impugned judgments.
Hence, I do - 16 - NC: 2024:KHC:45699 not find any error in the impugned judgments or any substantial question of law does not arise in this appeal.

14. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The appeal is dismissed.
The judgments and decrees passed by the courts below are hereby confirmed.
No order as to the costs.
